title: Human Tissue Slicing and Dissections for Nuclear Isolations
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bq6ymzfw
materials: Human Tissue Slicing and Dissections for Nuclear Isolations
Frozen Tissue block from ROI to be profiled
1M DL-Dithiothreitol solution (DTT) (Sigma BioUltra, molecular biology grade, 1M solution in water, 43816 or equivalent)
Peel-A-Way Rectangular Plastic Disposable Embedding Molds (VWR 15160-339)
Neurotrace 500/525 Nissl Stain (Thermo Fischer Scientific N21480)
250 ml RNase-free Glass Erlenmeyer flask (Sigma Z723088)
RNase free Dumont Fine-Tip Forceps (Roboz RS-5045)
RNase free Bracken Blunt-Tip Forceps (Roboz RS-5211)
Computer/laptop computer with image capture software installed

steps.title: Aliquot 1 M DTT stock
steps.instruction: Allow the received 1 M DTT solution to reach room temperature, shake until any precipitates dissolve, then dispense 3 ml aliquots into sterile 15 ml conical tubes, label, and freeze immediately at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 4 % agarose blocks
steps.instruction: Measure 100 ml nuclease‑free water (Ambion) into an RNase‑free glass Erlenmeyer flask, add 4 g agarose, microwave ~1 min at 50 % power, swirl, continue heating in 15‑20 s intervals until fully dissolved without bubbling, pour into plastic embedding molds, let set at room temperature or 4 °C, store blocks in a clean box or bag at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks.

steps.title: Make 10 mM DTT PBS buffer
steps.instruction: In a sterile 500 ml plastic bottle, combine 30 ml 10 X PBS (pH 7.4, Ambion) with 267 ml nuclease‑free water, add 3 ml thawed 1 M DTT, invert ~10 times, then place the bottle on ice or in a 4 °C fridge (or –20 °C for 20‑30 min) until ice‑cold.

steps.title: Prepare Nissl staining solution
steps.instruction: Using a serological pipette, transfer 20 ml of the ice‑cold 10 mM DTT PBS buffer to a sterile 50 ml conical tube, add 200 µl Neurotrace 500/525 Nissl stain (Thermo Fisher) and 100 µl RNasin Plus (final 0.5 % w/v, 0.2 U/µl), invert 5‑10 times (do not vortex), keep on ice; note Neurotrace contains DMSO and may be thawed at 45 °C for ~10 min if frozen, then returned to –20 °C after use.

steps.title: Decontaminate work area
steps.instruction: Spray all work surfaces and tools with RNase Away, wipe the vibratome chuck and bath with 70 % ethanol, wait ~5 min for evaporation, then keep the area RNase‑free.

steps.title: Set up petri dishes and plate
steps.instruction: Place a sterile 100 mm petri dish on ice and fill with cold 10 mM DTT PBS buffer, cover with lid; prepare a 24‑well plate by adding ~1 ml of the Nissl staining solution to each of 10‑12 wells, keep the plate on ice and covered when not in use.

steps.title: Prepare vibratome bath
steps.instruction: Insert the vibratome bath holder into its holder, fill with wet ice, cover with a 24‑well plate lid to prevent ice contamination, then slide the holder into place and tighten the side handle.

steps.title: Configure vibratome settings
steps.instruction: Turn on the vibratome, set slice thickness to 500 µm and speed to 0.12 mm/s.

steps.title: Trim and glue agarose block
steps.instruction: Remove a clean agarose block from the 4 °C fridge, cut away the plastic mold, trim sides to ~2‑4 × the tissue block size, dry the surface with a Kimwipe, apply a matching amount of superglue to the vibratome chuck and to the bottom half of the agarose block, place the block on the glue, let dry at room temperature for 3‑5 min.

steps.title: Thaw tissue block
steps.instruction: Remove the sealed bag containing the frozen tissue block from the –80 °C freezer, keep on dry ice, then cut open the bag with a clean razor and drop the block into the ice‑cold 10 mM DTT PBS buffer petri dish; allow to thaw for 1‑2 min until no visible ice remains.

steps.title: Trim tissue if needed
steps.instruction: If trimming is required, transfer the block with blunt‑tip forceps or a flat spatula to a clean petri dish lid, use disposable scalpels to remove excess white matter, pia, or irregular areas, creating a flat mounting surface.

steps.title: Mount tissue on agarose
steps.instruction: Apply a thin line of superglue to the front of the agarose block and to the side that will contact the tissue, dab the tissue briefly with a Kimwipe or filter paper (or a perforated spoon) to remove excess liquid, then position the tissue so that slices will be perpendicular to the pial surface; if the base is uneven, glue small agarose wedges to the chuck as supports.

steps.title: Dry mounting glue
steps.instruction: Place the vibratome mounting disk on the surface of ice and wait 2‑3 min for the glue to set.

steps.title: Fill bath with buffer
steps.instruction: Fill the vibratome bath with ice‑cold 10 mM DTT PBS buffer, creating a cold slurry.

steps.title: Insert chuck and blade
steps.instruction: Place the vibratome chuck with the mounted agarose‑tissue block into the bath (agarose side away from blade), use forceps to insert a clean ceramic blade into the holder, tighten with a hex wrench, lower the blade until the second white line on the far left is barely visible (use the check feature to calibrate if needed).

steps.title: Position blade above tissue
steps.instruction: Raise the stage by pressing the “Up” button until the blade is ~1‑5 mm above the tissue surface, set start and end positions, then advance the blade forward until it is close to the tissue and hold the cutting edge button to set the first window edge (light turns green).

steps.title: Define cutting window
steps.instruction: Advance the blade an additional 1‑5 mm past the agarose block, hold the cutting edge button again to set the second window edge (light turns green).

steps.title: Section tissue
steps.instruction: Press Run/Stop to begin sectioning; if the blade is too high, press Pause then Run/Stop twice to advance one 500 µm section, repeat until the blade reaches the tissue, then continue cutting the entire block.

steps.title: Collect sections
steps.instruction: Using a wide‑mouth transfer pipette, pick up each cut section and transfer it to a well of the 24‑well plate containing Nissl staining solution on ice, minimizing carry‑over of 1 M DTT; keep sections in staining solution for at least 5 min on ice.

steps.title: Dispose of used buffer
steps.instruction: After sectioning, pour the remaining 10 mM DTT PBS buffer into a secondary container labeled hazardous waste; combine any leftover Nissl staining solution with 10 mM DTT PBS buffer for disposal; EHS will handle hazardous waste.

steps.title: Decontaminate vibratome
steps.instruction: Place any remaining tissue pieces from the chuck into 10 % bleach for ≥20 min, then rinse chuck, bath, and holder with copious distilled water, spray with 70 % ethanol and wipe with a Kimwipe, clean all tools with 70 % ethanol and dry with a Kimwipe, discard the ceramic blade into a sharps container and wipe the blade holder with 70 % ethanol after rinsing with MilliQ water, finally turn off the vibratome.

steps.title: Prepare microdissection tubes
steps.instruction: Label individual 1.5 ml RNase‑free microcentrifuge tubes for each tissue layer and add ~500 µl of Nissl staining solution or 10 mM DTT PBS supplemented with 0.5 % RNasin Plus (or RNaseOUT); keep tubes on ice.

steps.title: Transfer slices to imaging dishes
steps.instruction: Using a wide‑mouth plastic pipette, move each stained slice to a sterile sylgard‑coated 35 mm petri dish containing 10 mM DTT PBS or fluorescent Nissl solution, then take a fluorescent image of each slice and return it to the 24‑well plate.

steps.title: Select optimal slices
steps.instruction: Choose slices with minimal damage, even 500 µm thickness, clear pia‑to‑white‑matter boundaries, and visible cortical layers; aim for at least two good slices, but a single high‑quality slice is acceptable.

steps.title: Microdissect cortical layers
steps.instruction: Place a selected slice into a sylgard‑coated small petri dish with ~1 ml cold 10 mM DTT PBS, use microdissection tools (microknife, forceps) and reference images to cut horizontal lines at each layer boundary, then make vertical cuts to isolate each layer from layer 1 through layer 6.

steps.title: Collect dissected layers
steps.instruction: Remove the tip of a P1000 pipette tip with a razor blade, use the opened tip and a P1000 pipette to transfer each dissected layer into its corresponding labeled microcentrifuge tube on ice; repeat for all layers and for any additional slices, reusing the widened tip as needed.

steps.title: Document dissections
steps.instruction: Photograph each dissected layer after transfer; keep tubes on ice until proceeding to nuclear isolation.

steps.title: Proceed to nuclear isolation
steps.instruction: When all samples are collected, continue with the Nuclear Isolation Protocol (PF0291).

steps.title: Final waste disposal
steps.instruction: Dispose of remaining 10 mM DTT PBS by pouring down the sink into the municipal sewer; treat 1 M DTT stock as hazardous waste and place in a properly labeled container for EHS disposal; place any remaining tissue from the vibratome mounting disk into 10 % bleach (50 ml conical tube) for ≥20 min, then discard in biohazard waste; place vibratome blade, razor, and scalpel in a sharps container, rinse the mounting disk, bath, and holder with distilled water followed by 70 % ethanol, and wipe down the vibratome and blade holder with 70 % ethanol.
